additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

info.persona: Ganelle Tucci, a solitary, curiosity‑driven designer who meticulously organizes their creative and financial worlds, fuels their imagination with ambient soundscapes, and balances a competitive edge with a habit of over‑booking sketch sessions at the cost of occasional social disengagement.
info.professional_persona: Ganelle Tucci, a senior graphic designer in Boston, blends rigorous visual communication expertise—mastery of Adobe Creative Suite, typographic theory, and generative AI experimentation—with a methodical, solitary workflow that fuels their competitive drive to craft culturally resonant brand narratives for museums and socially conscious clients.
info.cultural_background: Ganelle grew up in a middle‑class Italian‑American family in the Boston suburbs. Her upbringing combined the close‑knit traditions of her heritage—family meals, appreciation for craftsmanship, and storytelling—with the New England emphasis on education and historic preservation. Regular trips to the Museum of Fine Arts and the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum cultivated an early love for European masters, while her humanities studies deepened her understanding of cultural narratives. This blend of Italian cultural aesthetic sensibility and New England’s restrained, archival style informs her design choices, favoring elegant typographic pairings, a muted color palette, and visual references that honor both personal heritage and regional history.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime, Ganelle immerses herself in solitary, reflective activities. She frequently visits art museums and historic sites in the Boston area, sketches in her notebook, and experiments with watercolor and charcoal. An avid reader, she explores modern philosophy, art theory, and speculative fiction, often drawing inspiration for her designs. She also enjoys photography of architectural details, hiking quiet trails in nearby conservation areas, practicing yoga for mental focus, and curating playlists of ambient and experimental music to accompany her creative process.
info.sports_persona: Ganelle Tucci, an avid hiker of the Blue Hills Reservation and occasional participant in the Boston Marathon training group, channels their solitary energy into weekly trail runs and yoga, while quietly cheering for the Boston Celtics during the NBA season.
info.arts_persona: Ganelle Tucci, who spends weekends sketching in the Boston Museum of Fine Arts and curating ambient playlists featuring Brian Eno, Aphex Twin, and William Basinski, draws creative inspiration from the minimalist paintings of Agnes Martin and the light installations of James Turrell, integrating these influences into their own experimental watercolor and charcoal work.
info.travel_persona: Ganelle Tucci, a meticulous solo traveler, favors quiet, culture‑rich itineraries—such as a reflective weekend in Salem’s historic district, a design‑focused study tour of Florence’s Renaissance galleries, and a planned 2025 pilgrimage to Kyoto’s temples—balancing modest budget constraints with a willingness to invest in museum passes and local artisan workshops.
info.culinary_persona: Ganelle Tucci, whose culinary experiments range from a precisely plated roasted beet and goat‑cheese salad seasoned with sumac to a comforting miso‑ramen bowl featuring black garlic and hand‑rolled noodles, enjoys cooking at a moderate skill level while frequently sourcing seasonal produce at the Boston Public Market and savoring a single‑origin espresso after dinner.

info.persona: Santiago Jacob blends a practical, structure‑loving work ethic with a sociable, community‑focused lifestyle, punctuated by weekly soccer, weekend hikes, homemade Mexican feasts, and a steady march toward a logistics supervisory role.
info.professional_persona: Santiago Jacob, a seasoned shipping and receiving clerk with mastery of warehouse management systems and forklift operation, leverages their practical, detail‑oriented mindset and love of structured processes to streamline inventory control while mentoring newcomers, aiming to step into a supervisory role within the next five years.
info.cultural_background: Santiago was born and raised in a Mexican-American family on the U.S.-Mexico border. Growing up in El Paso, he was immersed in a bilingual environment, speaking both Spanish and English at home and in the community. His family maintains strong ties to Mexican traditions, celebrating holidays such as Cinco de Mayo, Día de los Muertos, and Christmas with a blend of Mexican and Texan customs. He learned to cook family recipes passed down through generations and values the importance of family gatherings and community solidarity. The cross-border culture of El Paso, with its rich blend of American and Mexican influences, shapes his worldview, fostering respect for cultural diversity, a strong sense of hospitality, and a commitment to preserving his heritage while engaging with the broader Texan community.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Santiago enjoys a mix of active and cultural hobbies that keep him connected to his community. He regularly joins a local soccer league, where he plays as a midfielder and values teamwork. He also loves cooking traditional Mexican dishes like tamales, pozole, and homemade salsa, often sharing meals with friends and neighbors. On weekends, he hikes the trails of the Franklin Mountains and fishes along the Rio Grande. He has a keen interest in Norteño and Tejano music, attends local festivals, and participates in the annual Día de los Muertos celebrations by helping organize community altars. Additionally, Santiago volunteers at a neighborhood food bank and occasionally attends church gatherings.
info.sports_persona: Santiago Jacob energizes weekends as a midfielder for a local soccer league, roots for El Paso Locomotive FC and follows the Mexican national team, hikes the Franklin Mountains with a club, and casts a line along the Rio Grande, blending team spirit with solo outdoor pursuits.
info.arts_persona: Santiago Jacob immerses themselves in Norteño and Tejano sounds, regularly attending concerts featuring Ramón Ayala, Los Tigres del Norte, and Selena tributes at the El Paso County Coliseum, while also helping organize community altars for Día de los Muertos, reflecting a deep cultural artistic passion.
info.travel_persona: Santiago Jacob prefers road‑trip adventures, planning weekend getaways to Big Bend National Park, Carlsbad Caverns, and a nostalgic stretch along historic Route 66, while dreaming of a culinary pilgrimage to Oaxaca to study traditional mole recipes, balancing budget constraints with a love of scenic drives.
info.culinary_persona: Santiago Jacob delights in preparing tamales, pozole, and a fiery homemade salsa using masa harina, dried chiles, pork shoulder, fresh cilantro, and epazote, often experimenting with corn husks and sharing these hearty meals with friends and neighbors, though they sometimes over‑season to the point of heat overload.

info.persona: Taylor Pearson is a competitively driven, detail‑oriented administrator whose love of gardening, yoga, and structured problem‑solving masks a chronic worry habit; they also have a penchant for meticulous budget spreadsheets.
info.professional_persona: Taylor Pearson is a seasoned office administration specialist; they draw on two decades of workflow optimization, meticulous record‑keeping, and a skeptical yet data‑driven evaluation style to lead clerical teams toward measurable efficiency gains, championing competitive performance benchmarks while aspiring to senior management.
info.cultural_background: Taylor grew up in a small town in western Michigan within a white, largely German‑American community that values hard work, self‑reliance, and modesty. Her family emphasized punctuality, practicality, and community service, shaping her pragmatic outlook and competitive spirit. Raised in the Midwest, she internalized a balanced approach to tradition and innovation, which is reflected in her willingness to try new ideas while respecting proven methods. Although never married, she maintains close ties with extended family and local neighbors, often participating in community events and church gatherings that celebrate regional heritage. Her education at a local community college equipped her with an associate’s degree in business‑related studies, reinforcing the regional emphasis on accessible, practical education.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her downtime Taylor enjoys gardening in her backyard, finding the balance of nurturing plants both calming and productive. She frequently walks the trails along the Grand River and explores local state parks, which offers both solitude and gentle exercise. An avid reader, she prefers non‑fiction books on productivity, psychology, and self‑improvement, but occasionally indulges in classic mystery novels. Cooking new recipes, especially seasonal dishes from the farmers’ market, satisfies her curiosity while staying practical. To combat stress, she practices yoga twice a week, does crossword puzzles and Sudoku, and keeps a daily journal. Volunteering at the community food bank and knitting scarves for seniors are ways she stays connected to her community.
info.sports_persona: Taylor Pearson follows the Detroit Lions, Detroit Tigers, and Michigan State Spartans football teams; they join the Grand River Trail Running Club for weekend jogs, play casual tennis at the local community center, and treat fitness as a low‑stress counterbalance to a competitive work mindset.
info.arts_persona: Taylor Pearson enjoys the timeless mysteries of Agatha Christie, the classic cinema of Alfred Hitchcock, and the folk storytelling of Tracy Chapman; they regularly attend the community theater's productions of Shakespeare, finding these artistic experiences a soothing antidote to daily stress.
info.travel_persona: Taylor Pearson prefers meticulously planned road trips to nearby Midwestern gems like Mackinac Island and the Great Lakes shoreline, while also dreaming of a relaxed culinary tour of Tuscany’s vineyards; they balance adventure with a modest budget and occasional family obligations.
info.culinary_persona: Taylor Pearson delights in crafting seasonal farmer‑market meals such as roasted heirloom carrots with thyme, beet‑goat cheese salad with walnuts, and apple‑cinnamon crisp; they boast a solid home‑cook skill set that mixes straightforward preparation with occasional experimental spice blends like smoked paprika.
